title: Length: Measuring in Centimetres and Metres
seo_title: Length – Primary 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Compare and measure lengths using non-standard units and centimetres and metres; solve length problems. (summary of the NERDC Primary 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 maths worksheets on length: comparing lengths, measuring with a ruler in centimetres, metres, and length word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Short things in cm, long things in m.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • We measure length with a ruler or a tape measure.
  • Short things are measured in centimetres (cm). Long things are measured in metres (m).
  • Put the 0 of the ruler at the end of the object.

Examples

Example

A ribbon is 25 cm. Another is 18 cm.

25 − 18

Answer: 7 cm longer

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Starting at 1 on the rulerStart at 0.
Using cm for a long roadUse metres or kilometres.
Not lining up the endsLine up one end at 0.

faq.q: What do we use to measure length?
faq.a: A ruler or a tape measure.

faq.q: What is longer, 1 m or 50 cm?

items.q: How many cubes long is the crayon?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the crayon to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the cubes. How long is the key?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the key to the other: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: How many cubes long is the pencil?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the pencil to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. It is 7 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the rubber?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the rubber to the other: 1, 2. It is 2 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: How many cubes long is the ribbon?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the ribbon to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It is 5 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: You measure a crayon with cubes. What do you count?
c: all the cubes in the box
items.e: Lay cubes along the crayon from end to end. Count only the cubes under the crayon. That number is its length.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the leaf?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the leaf to the other: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: How many cubes long is the straw?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the straw to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. It is 9 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the felt-tip pen?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the felt-tip pen to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: How many cubes long is the caterpillar?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the caterpillar to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. It is 6 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The pencil goes further, so it is longer. The pencil is longer.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The straw goes further, so it is longer. The straw is longer.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The pencil goes further, so it is longer. The nail is shorter.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The ribbon goes further, so it is longer. The rubber is shorter.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Both end at the same place. They are the same length.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The lolly stick goes further, so it is longer. The lolly stick is longer.

items.q: Which is taller?
items.e: Both stand on the floor. Look at the tops. The pencil reaches higher, so it is taller. The pencil is taller.

items.q: Which is taller?
items.e: Both stand on the floor. Look at the tops. The straw reaches higher, so it is taller. The straw is taller.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure the length of a pencil?
items.e: A pencil is short. It fits on a ruler, so use centimetres.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure the length of the school hall?
items.e: The hall is long. Use metres for long things.

items.q: Which unit would you use to measure how tall a tree is?
items.e: A tree is tall. Use metres. Kilograms and litres do not measure length.

items.q: Ikenna puts one end of his pencil on 1, not on 0. The other end is on 8. How long is the pencil?
items.e: The pencil starts at 1, so 8 is not the answer. 8 − 1 = 7. The pencil is 7 cm long.

items.q: How much longer is the pencil than the crayon?
items.e: Both start at 0. The pencil ends at 14 and the crayon ends at 9. Count the spaces from 9 to 14, or subtract: 14 − 9 = 5. The pencil is 5 centimetres longer.

items.q: How much longer is the craft stick than the caterpillar?
items.e: Both start at 0. The craft stick ends at 11 and the caterpillar ends at 4. Count the spaces from 4 to 11, or subtract: 11 − 4 = 7. The craft stick is 7 centimetres longer.

items.q: How much longer is the leaf than the paper clip?
items.e: Both start at 0. The leaf ends at 12 and the paper clip ends at 3. Count the spaces from 3 to 12, or subtract: 12 − 3 = 9. The leaf is 9 centimetres longer.

items.q: How much shorter is the nail than the ribbon?
items.e: Both start at 0. The ribbon ends at 15 and the nail ends at 7. Count the spaces from 7 to 15, or subtract: 15 − 7 = 8. The nail is 8 centimetres shorter.

items.q: A pencil is 18 centimetres long. A crayon is 9 centimetres long. How much longer is the pencil?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 18 − 9 = 9. Do not add the lengths: 18 + 9 = 27 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Ifeanyi found two worms. One is 12 centimetres long. The other is 7 centimetres long. How much longer is the long worm?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 12 − 7 = 5. Or count up from 7 to 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Do not add the lengths: 12 + 7 = 19 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: A pool is 25 metres long. Tobi swims 18 metres and stops. How many more metres must he swim to reach the end?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 25 − 18 = 7. Check by adding: 18 + 7 = 25. Do not add the lengths: 25 + 18 = 43 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Simi's block tower is 54 centimetres tall. Temi's tower is 29 centimetres tall. How much taller is Simi's tower?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 54 − 29 = 25. Check by adding: 29 + 25 = 54. Do not add the lengths: 54 + 29 = 83 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: A sunflower is 85 centimetres tall. A tomato plant is 47 centimetres tall. How much taller is the sunflower?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 85 − 47 = 38. Check by adding: 47 + 38 = 85. Do not add the lengths: 85 + 47 = 132 is the total, not the difference.

items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 12 − 7 = 5. Or count up from 7 to 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Do not add the lengths: 12 + 7 = 19 is the total, not the difference.

items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 25 − 18 = 7. Check by adding: 18 + 7 = 25. Do not add the lengths: 25 + 18 = 43 is the total, not the difference.

items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 54 − 29 = 25. Check by adding: 29 + 25 = 54. Do not add the lengths: 54 + 29 = 83 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Victor's block tower is 54 centimetres tall. Ibrahim's tower is 29 centimetres tall. How much taller is Victor's tower?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 54 − 29 = 25. Check by adding: 29 + 25 = 54. Do not add the lengths: 54 + 29 = 83 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: A pool is 25 metres long. Yusuf swims 18 metres and stops. How many more metres must he swim to reach the end?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 25 − 18 = 7. Check by adding: 18 + 7 = 25. Do not add the lengths: 25 + 18 = 43 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: A worm crawled 27 centimetres. Then it crawled 21 centimetres more. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The two lengths are put together, so add: 27 + 21 = ☐. 27 + 21 = 48, so the total is 48 centimetres.

items.q: Uju swam 25 metres. Then she swam 27 more metres. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The two lengths are put together, so add: 25 + 27 = ☐. 25 + 27 = 52, so the total is 52 metres.

items.q: Bisi built a block tower 35 centimetres tall. Then she added blocks to make it 26 centimetres taller. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The two lengths are put together, so add: 35 + 26 = ☐. 35 + 26 = 61, so the total is 61 centimetres.

items.q: The class paints a red line 39 metres long on the playground. Then they paint a blue line 31 metres long at the end of it. How long are the two lines together?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 39 + 31 = ☐. 39 + 30 = 69. Then 69 + 1 = 70. (9 + 1 units make a new ten.) Answer: 70 metres.

items.q: A bean plant was 23 centimetres tall. It grew 13 centimetres this month. How tall is the bean plant now?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 23 + 13 = ☐. 23 + 10 = 33. Then 33 + 3 = 36. Answer: 36 centimetres.

items.q: Peter rides his bike 34 metres to a friend's house. Then he rides 39 metres to school. How far does Peter ride in all?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 34 + 39 = ☐. 34 + 30 = 64. Then 64 + 9 = 73. (4 + 9 units make a new ten.) Answer: 73 metres.

items.q: Chioma lays a pencil and a crayon end to end. The pencil is 14 centimetres long. The crayon is 7 centimetres long. How long are they together?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 14 + 7 = ☐. 14 + 7 = 21. (4 + 7 units make a new ten.) Answer: 21 centimetres.

items.q: Nonso walks 38 metres to the corner. Then he walks 39 metres to the park. How far does he walk in all?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 38 + 39 = ☐. 38 + 30 = 68. Then 68 + 9 = 77. (8 + 9 units make a new ten.) Answer: 77 metres.

items.q: Simi has a red ribbon 31 centimetres long and a blue ribbon 21 centimetres long. She tapes them end to end. How long is the new ribbon?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 31 + 21 = ☐. 31 + 20 = 51. Then 51 + 1 = 52. Answer: 52 centimetres.

items.q: A toy train has three cars. The cars are 16 centimetres, 17 centimetres and 13 centimetres long. How long is the train?
items.e: Add all three lengths: 16 + 17 + 13 = ☐. First 16 + 17 = 33. Then 33 + 13 = 46. Answer: 46 centimetres.

items.q: A candle was 26 centimetres tall. It burned down 12 centimetres. How tall is the candle now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 26 − 12 = ☐. 26 − 10 = 16. Then 16 − 2 = 14. Check: 14 + 12 = 26. Answer: 14 centimetres.

items.q: Kayode has to walk 91 metres to the library. He has walked 26 metres so far. How much farther does he have to walk?
items.e: You know the whole way and the part already walked. Subtract to find the part still to go: 91 − 26 = ☐. 91 − 20 = 71. Then 71 − 6 = 65. Check: 65 + 26 = 91. Answer: 65 metres.

items.q: A string is 81 centimetres long. Tunde uses 32 centimetres to make a necklace. How much string is left?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 81 − 32 = ☐. 81 − 30 = 51. Then 51 − 2 = 49. Check: 49 + 32 = 81. Answer: 49 centimetres.

items.q: A rope is 73 centimetres long. Chiamaka cuts off 31 centimetres. How long is the rope now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 73 − 31 = ☐. 73 − 30 = 43. Then 43 − 1 = 42. Check: 42 + 31 = 73. Answer: 42 centimetres.

items.q: A race is 99 metres long. Temi has run 45 metres. How many more metres does she need to run?
items.e: You know the whole race and the part already run. Subtract to find the part still to run: 99 − 45 = ☐. 99 − 40 = 59. Then 59 − 5 = 54. Check: 54 + 45 = 99. Answer: 54 metres.

items.q: A green toy snake is 85 centimetres long. A red toy snake is 36 centimetres long. How much longer is the green snake?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 85 − 36 = ☐. 85 − 30 = 55. Then 55 − 6 = 49. Check: 36 + 49 = 85. Answer: 49 centimetres.

items.q: A blue ribbon is 77 centimetres long. A red ribbon is 15 centimetres shorter than the blue ribbon. How long is the red ribbon?
items.e: The red ribbon is shorter, so subtract: 77 − 15 = ☐. 77 − 10 = 67. Then 67 − 5 = 62. Answer: 62 centimetres.

items.q: The big pool is 25 metres long. The small pool is 8 metres long. How much shorter is the small pool?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 25 − 8 = ☐. 25 − 8 = 17. Check: 8 + 17 = 25. Answer: 17 metres. “How much shorter” is the same difference.

items.q: Fatima has to walk 88 metres to the library. She has walked 54 metres so far. How much farther does she have to walk?
items.e: You know the whole way and the part already walked. Subtract to find the part still to go: 88 − 54 = ☐. 88 − 50 = 38. Then 38 − 4 = 34. Check: 34 + 54 = 88. Answer: 34 metres.

items.q: A candle was 34 centimetres tall. It burned down 15 centimetres. How tall is the candle now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 34 − 15 = ☐. 34 − 10 = 24. Then 24 − 5 = 19. Check: 19 + 15 = 34. Answer: 19 centimetres.

items.q: Start at 45. Jump 20 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 45 and move 20 spaces: 45 + 20 = ☐. 45 + 20 = 65.

items.q: Start at 23. Jump 30 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 23 and move 30 spaces: 23 + 30 = ☐. 23 + 30 = 53.

items.q: Start at 58. Jump 14 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 58 and move 14 spaces: 58 + 14 = ☐. 58 + 10 = 68. Then 68 + 4 = 72.

items.q: Start at 36. Jump 25 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 36 and move 25 spaces: 36 + 25 = ☐. 36 + 20 = 56. Then 56 + 5 = 61.

items.q: Start at 17. Jump 18 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 17 and move 18 spaces: 17 + 18 = ☐. 17 + 10 = 27. Then 27 + 8 = 35.

items.q: Start at 64. Jump 27 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 64 and move 27 spaces: 64 + 27 = ☐. 64 + 20 = 84. Then 84 + 7 = 91.

items.q: Start at 72. Jump 30 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 72 and move back 30 spaces: 72 − 30 = ☐. 72 − 30 = 42.

items.q: Start at 55. Jump 16 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 55 and move back 16 spaces: 55 − 16 = ☐. 55 − 10 = 45. Then 45 − 6 = 39.

items.q: Start at 81. Jump 25 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 81 and move back 25 spaces: 81 − 25 = ☐. 81 − 20 = 61. Then 61 − 5 = 56.

items.q: Start at 46. Jump 19 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 46 and move back 19 spaces: 46 − 19 = ☐. 46 − 10 = 36. Then 36 − 9 = 27.

items.q: Start at 90. Jump 37 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 90 and move back 37 spaces: 90 − 37 = ☐. 90 − 30 = 60. Then 60 − 7 = 53.

items.q: How long is the jump from 34 to 52?
items.e: Count up from 34 to 52, or subtract: 52 − 34 = 18. Check: 34 + 18 = 52. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the jump from 48 to 75?
items.e: Count up from 48 to 75, or subtract: 75 − 48 = 27. Check: 48 + 27 = 75. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the jump from 26 to 41?
items.e: Count up from 26 to 41, or subtract: 41 − 26 = 15. Check: 26 + 15 = 41. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the jump from 57 to 83?
items.e: Count up from 57 to 83, or subtract: 83 − 57 = 26. Check: 57 + 26 = 83. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Which equation does the number line show?
items.e: The jumps are +20 and +5. Together they make 25. Start at 30 and add 25: 30 + 25 = 55.

items.q: Which equation does the number line show?
items.e: The jumps are +20 and +8. Together they make 28. Start at 43 and add 28: 43 + 28 = 71.

items.q: Which equation does the number line show?
items.e: Both jumps go left, so subtract. −20 and −6 make −26: 74 − 26 = 48.

items.q: Which number line shows 30 + 25?
items.e: Number line D starts at 30 and jumps 25 to the right, to 55. 30 + 25 = 55.

items.q: Which number line shows 62 − 24?
items.e: Number line B starts at 62 and jumps 24 to the left, to 38. 62 − 24 = 38.
